## Services

---

- [Political PR & Image Building](https://publicpulse.com.bd/services/political-pr): Public Pulse Agency runs end-to-end political PR campaigns for Bangladeshi candidates and parties — candidate image building, narrative engineering, opposition research, crisis communication, and a five-phase election execution from pre-campaign positioning to post-election PR. Based in Dhaka, serving constituencies nationwide.
- [Social Media Management](https://publicpulse.com.bd/services/social-media): Public Pulse Agency manages Facebook, Instagram, YouTube and TikTok accounts for Bangladeshi brands — content strategy, weekly posting calendars, Bangla and English community management, paid amplification, and monthly growth reports. We treat social as a sales channel, not a vanity surface.
- [Content Production](https://publicpulse.com.bd/services/content-production): Public Pulse Agency produces brand films, social cutdowns, photography, motion graphics, drone footage and UGC content for Bangladeshi brands — shot in Dhaka, Cox's Bazar, Sylhet and on location across the country. Strategy-first scripts, weekly delivery cadence, and content built for the platforms it will actually live on.
- [Paid Ads & Campaigns](https://publicpulse.com.bd/services/paid-ads): Public Pulse Agency runs paid-media campaigns on Meta, Google and YouTube for Bangladeshi advertisers — full account build, Pixel and Conversion API setup, daily bid and creative optimization, weekly ROAS reports. We work to a return-on-ad-spend target, not impressions, and report in BDT against your CFO's numbers.
- [Hospitality Marketing](https://publicpulse.com.bd/services/hospitality): Public Pulse Agency markets Bangladeshi resorts, hotels and restaurants — Cox's Bazar to Sylhet, Dhaka to Chittagong. OTA listing optimization, Google Business Profile, food-delivery platform management, video tours, and paid campaigns that fill rooms and tables on the calendar dates that need filling.
- [Brand Building & Design](https://publicpulse.com.bd/services/brand-building): Public Pulse Agency builds brand identities for Bangladeshi startups and rebrands for established businesses — naming, logo, visual identity, packaging, brand voice guidelines, and a positioning map against your real competitors. The output is a brand book your team can actually apply, not a moodboard that lives in a Drive folder.
- [SEO & Website Development](https://publicpulse.com.bd/services/seo-website): Public Pulse Agency runs SEO and builds websites for Bangladeshi businesses — local SEO, technical SEO, on-page optimization, schema markup, and conversion-focused website builds in Next.js or WordPress. We aim for traffic that converts, not traffic that bounces, and we measure rankings against the queries your customers actually type.
- [Analytics & Performance Reporting](https://publicpulse.com.bd/services/analytics-reporting): Public Pulse Agency sets up GA4, Google Tag Manager, Meta Pixel and Conversion API for Bangladeshi advertisers, then builds Looker Studio dashboards that surface marketing ROI in BDT against revenue. Monthly reports that pass an audit — and that your CFO will actually read instead of forwarding to the marketing team for translation.
- [Influencer & KOL Marketing](https://publicpulse.com.bd/services/influencer-marketing): Public Pulse Agency runs influencer and KOL campaigns across Bangladesh — discovery from a vetted creator pool, tier strategy from nano to macro, contracts and briefs, FTC-compliant disclosure, and tracked performance with verified results. We treat influencer as a measurable acquisition channel, not a goodwill spend.

## Guides (HowTo playbooks)

---

- [How to run a Facebook ad campaign for a Bangladesh constituency election](https://publicpulse.com.bd/guides/facebook-campaign-bd-election): Before anything else, complete Meta ad authorization (identity + location) and register the “Paid for by” disclaimer — political ads are rejected without them. Then pin a geo-radius to the constituency, run Bangla-first creative within Special Ad Category limits, back it with CAPI, and heavy-weight budget in the final 14 days. Full offer: /political-facebook-ads-bangladesh.
- [Set up Meta Conversions API for a Bangladesh e-commerce site](https://publicpulse.com.bd/guides/meta-conversions-api-setup): Meta Conversions API is server-to-server event tracking from your site to Meta — recovering the 30–50% of conversion signal that browser pixels lose to iOS ATT and ad blockers. Setup is one-time, takes about an hour, and is essential for Bangladesh e-commerce where COD pushes the last-mile event off-site entirely.
- [Add IndexNow to your publish pipeline](https://publicpulse.com.bd/guides/indexnow-publish-pipeline): IndexNow is an open protocol that lets your site instantly notify Bing, Yandex and consortium engines when URLs publish, update, or delete. Setup is one key file at /indexnow-key.txt plus a single HTTP POST on every publish. Google doesn't participate but Bing-backed search covers most of the rest.

## Comparisons

---

- [Agency vs in-house marketing team — which makes sense for a Bangladesh brand?](https://publicpulse.com.bd/compare/agency-vs-in-house-marketing-bangladesh): Below BDT 5 lakh/month total marketing spend, an integrated agency is more honest economically — you get strategy + creative + paid + analytics for the salary of one mid-level manager. Above BDT 15 lakh/month with stable channel mix, in-house starts to win on speed-of-iteration and brand depth.
- [Facebook Ads vs Google Ads — which works better in Bangladesh?](https://publicpulse.com.bd/compare/facebook-vs-google-ads-bangladesh): Facebook still drives more reach + conversions for most Bangladesh consumer brands because of dominant social usage + DTC + Foodpanda-style discovery. Google Ads outperforms for high-intent verticals (B2B, real estate, education enquiry, healthcare appointments) where someone is actively searching.
- [Boosting vs Ads Manager for political campaigns in Bangladesh](https://publicpulse.com.bd/compare/boosting-vs-ads-manager-political): For a political campaign in Bangladesh, Ads Manager is the engine and boosting is the moment-rider. Ads Manager gives real audiences, message variants, frequency control, and daily optimization; boosting just amplifies one post fast. Both are only legitimate from an authorized, disclaimed account. Most winning constituencies use both — Ads Manager to carry the message, boosting to ride a spike.

## Glossary (canonical BD definitions)

---

- [Answer Block](https://publicpulse.com.bd/glossary/answer-block): An answer block is a short, self-contained answer of 40–60 words placed at the top of a long-form page. AI engines such as Google AI Overviews, ChatGPT, Claude and Perplexity can lift it verbatim, so it gives them a complete, citable answer in the page's first viewport instead of synthesizing one from elsewhere.
- [AEO (Answer Engine Optimization)](https://publicpulse.com.bd/glossary/aeo): Answer Engine Optimization is the practice of structuring a page so AI-driven answer engines, including Google AI Overviews, Bing Copilot and voice assistants, cite it as the source for direct answers. It combines answer-first prose with explicit JSON-LD, such as FAQPage, HowTo or DefinedTerm, and factual accuracy.
- [GEO (Generative Engine Optimization)](https://publicpulse.com.bd/glossary/geo): Generative Engine Optimization is the practice of making a page easy for generative engines such as ChatGPT, Claude, Perplexity and Gemini to ground their answers in. It requires content that LLM crawlers like GPTBot, ClaudeBot and PerplexityBot can index, written with specific dated facts and plain-language explainers.
- [FAQPage Schema](https://publicpulse.com.bd/glossary/faqpage-schema): FAQPage is a schema.org JSON-LD type that marks up a page's FAQ section, telling search engines exactly which question and answer pairs to consider for rich snippets and AI citations. Each pair should match how real users phrase their queries: short, conversational and written in their own language.
- [JSON-LD Schema](https://publicpulse.com.bd/glossary/schema-jsonld): JSON-LD schema is structured data embedded in a <script type='application/ld+json'> tag that describes a page's entities, such as Service, Article, Organization and FAQPage, for machines. Valid markup uses stable @id URIs that cross-reference the Organization, because field omissions silently remove a page's eligibility for rich results.
- [llms.txt](https://publicpulse.com.bd/glossary/llms-txt): llms.txt is a plain-text file at /llms.txt that gives AI engines a curated, link-rich summary of a site to ground from, analogous to robots.txt for crawlers. It follows the llmstxt.org convention, and a companion /llms-full.txt carries the concatenated full text. Both should serve HTTP 200 directly, never redirects.
- [robots.txt](https://publicpulse.com.bd/glossary/robots-txt): robots.txt is a plain-text file at /robots.txt that tells crawlers which paths they are allowed to fetch. It can explicitly allow named crawlers, such as GPTBot, ClaudeBot, PerplexityBot, Google-Extended and Bingbot, and disallow private paths like /manage. Allowing AI crawlers is a deliberate choice so pages can be cited in AI answers.
- [Speakable](https://publicpulse.com.bd/glossary/speakable): Speakable is a schema.org property on Article that tells voice assistants such as Google Assistant and Alexa which CSS selector contains the answer to read aloud. Setting speakable.cssSelector to ['.answer-block'] points them at a 40–60 word answer block rather than random body copy, so the class name must stay in sync with the schema.
- [Political PR](https://publicpulse.com.bd/glossary/political-pr): Political PR is the public communications strategy for political candidates, parties and elected officials, covering candidate image-building, narrative engineering, opposition research and crisis communications. In Bangladesh it runs on a five-phase election cycle: pre-campaign positioning, ground research, narrative launch, polling-day execution and post-election PR. Public Pulse runs all five phases.
- [Narrative Engineering](https://publicpulse.com.bd/glossary/narrative-engineering): Narrative engineering is the deliberate construction of a campaign's core message, tested against constituency demographics and refined for sticking power. A narrative is not a slogan but a story arc: what the candidate stands for, what they oppose and what changes if they win, built to be retold by voters in their own words.
- [Opposition Research](https://publicpulse.com.bd/glossary/opposition-research): Opposition research is the systematic gathering of intelligence on an opponent's record, statements, vulnerabilities and likely lines of attack. Done responsibly, it relies on published statements, public records and verifiable claims. It is used to anticipate threats and to brief the candidate's own counter-messaging, never to seed disinformation.
- [Meta Conversions API (CAPI)](https://publicpulse.com.bd/glossary/meta-conversions-api): Meta Conversions API (CAPI) is server-to-server event tracking that sends conversions from a site or CRM to Meta's ad platform, recovering signal lost to iOS ATT and ad blockers. Because browser-side pixel firing drops 30–50% or more of events after iOS 14.5, sending the same events from the server gives Meta's bidding a more complete signal.
- [ROAS (Return on Ad Spend)](https://publicpulse.com.bd/glossary/roas): ROAS, or Return on Ad Spend, is the revenue generated for every BDT spent on advertising; a ROAS of 4× means BDT 4 of revenue per BDT 1 of ad spend. It is the headline metric for e-commerce paid media, but in isolation it can mislead, so it should be read alongside the new-versus-returning customer split.
- [CTR (Click-Through Rate)](https://publicpulse.com.bd/glossary/ctr): Click-through rate (CTR) is the fraction of ad impressions that became clicks, calculated as clicks ÷ impressions × 100. Benchmarks vary by placement: a 1% CTR on Meta feed is industry average, while the same figure on a search ad is poor. CTR works as a creative-quality signal, but downstream conversion rate is the goal.
- [IndexNow](https://publicpulse.com.bd/glossary/indexnow): IndexNow is an open protocol that lets a site instantly notify participating search engines, including Bing, Yandex and Seznam, when a URL is published, updated or deleted, bypassing crawl-budget delays. Google does not participate, but the major Bing-backed engines do, so publishers send the affected URLs on every publish action.
- [Speakable Schema](https://publicpulse.com.bd/glossary/speakable-schema): Speakable schema is the schema.org SpeakableSpecification, placed on Article or WebPage JSON-LD with a cssSelector that points voice assistants at the prose they should read aloud as the answer. The selector should target a 40–60 word self-contained answer, because longer passages get truncated mid-sentence on the device.
- [First-Party Data](https://publicpulse.com.bd/glossary/first-party-data): First-party data is customer data a business collected directly from its own site, app, CRM, point-of-sale or call centre, as opposed to third-party data bought from brokers or rented from ad platforms. It is the strategic asset for Bangladeshi brands as Meta and Google narrow third-party signal through iOS ATT and cookie deprecation.
- [Attribution Window](https://publicpulse.com.bd/glossary/attribution-window): The look-back period an ad platform credits an ad with a conversion — e.g. a 7-day-click 1-day-view window means Meta will count a purchase as the ad's outcome if it happens within 7 days of a click or 1 day of a view.
- [Engagement Rate](https://publicpulse.com.bd/glossary/engagement-rate): Engagement rate is the fraction of an audience that interacted with a piece of content through likes, comments, shares, saves or click-throughs, usually expressed as engagements ÷ reach × 100. It is the dominant proxy for organic content health on Facebook and Instagram, and should be kept separate from paid CTR and conversion rate.
- [Core Web Vitals](https://publicpulse.com.bd/glossary/core-web-vitals): Core Web Vitals are Google's three page-experience metrics: LCP (largest contentful paint, load speed), INP (interaction to next paint, responsiveness) and CLS (cumulative layout shift, visual stability). They act as a ranking signal and appear in Search Console. Pass thresholds: LCP ≤ 2.5s, INP ≤ 200ms, CLS ≤ 0.1.
- [Conversion API](https://publicpulse.com.bd/glossary/conversion-api): A conversion API is a server-to-server event protocol, such as Meta's Conversions API, Google's Enhanced Conversions or TikTok's Events API, that sends conversion data from the brand's server straight to the ad platform. It bypasses browser tracking that iOS ATT and ad blockers degrade, restoring 30–50% of the lost conversion signal.
- [Boosted Post](https://publicpulse.com.bd/glossary/boosted-post): A boosted post is a Facebook or Instagram post that is paid to reach more people, making it the simplest Meta ad. It offers limited targeting, one creative and no frequency control. When the content is political, a boosted post still requires ad authorization and a “Paid for by” disclaimer.
- [Ad Authorization](https://publicpulse.com.bd/glossary/ad-authorization): Ad authorization is Meta’s identity and location verification that an advertiser must complete before running ads about elections, politics or social issues. The advertiser confirms a verified identity and an in-country location and registers who is paying. Without it political ads are rejected, and it can take days to complete.
- [“Paid for by” Disclaimer](https://publicpulse.com.bd/glossary/paid-for-by-disclaimer): The “Paid for by” disclaimer is the mandatory label on every political ad naming who paid for it. Registered once during authorization on an authorized account, it is then applied automatically to every ad the campaign runs, and it feeds the public Ad Library where anyone can see what a candidate is running.
- [Special Ad Category](https://publicpulse.com.bd/glossary/special-ad-category): Special Ad Category is Meta’s restricted classification for political, electoral and social-issue ads. It limits targeting, so advertisers cannot narrow by age, gender, detailed demographics or many interest traits the way commercial ads allow. Campaigns instead build reach on geography and legitimate affinity, and must be designed to perform inside these limits.
- [Constituency Targeting](https://publicpulse.com.bd/glossary/constituency-targeting): Constituency targeting focuses paid Facebook reach on a specific electoral seat using Meta’s geography and affinity layers, within Special Ad Category limits. It tunes the location radius to union, ward and upazila lines and weights spend toward the pockets that decide the seat, targeting the voters who decide the margin rather than vanity reach.
